$comment: Shared test vectors for the weekly cap, RULE-20 (Scope §4.4–4.5).
These vectors are the contract between the TypeScript implementation in
packages/domain/cap.ts and the SQL function weekly_cap(...) that
weekly_cap_hours(staff, date) is built on. Both must produce the same
cap AND the same band for every case here. Owned by the `compliance` bot.
The four dimensions come straight off the §4.4 table:
visaLimited                — the worker is on the International student branch
termState                  — where the Mon-Sun week sits against the HOLIDAY
ranges read off the University Term Dates Letter
('none' = no ranges on file at all, which reads as
term time because every day falls outside every
holiday range)
completionLetterVerified   — §4.5 graduation, effective-dated from verification
optOut48h                  — the Working Time Regulations tick box
Two rules decide every row below:
A Mon-Sun week that straddles term and holiday takes the LOWER cap.
The opt-out lifts the 48 h ceiling everywhere EXCEPT where a visa condition
sets the limit (student, in term, not yet graduated) - §4.4 opt-out table.
supabase/tests/_shared/cap_vectors.psql is GENERATED from this file by
supabase/tests/_shared/cap-vectors.mjs. Re-run it after any edit here:
node supabase/tests/_shared/cap-vectors.mjs
The Vitest suite fails if the generated file has drifted.
--- University Completion Letter Requirement (docs/scope/) ---
Six further dimensions, all optional. Omit them and every case above is
unchanged, which is why the original fifteen carry none of them:
weekStart            - Monday of the week being asked about; the dated
facts below are meaningless without it
belowDegreeLevel     - the Student condition is 10 h, not 20
completionDate       - the release runs from the course completion date,
NOT from the day a manager verified the letter
visaExpiry           - inclusive; outranks everything, completion letter
included
optOutCancelledFrom  - end of the notice period, not the day notice was
given
under18              - cannot sign an opt-out, so a recorded tick is not
a valid one
A week straddling the completion date, or the end of an opt-out notice
period, takes the LOWER cap - the same principle RULE-20 already applies
to a week straddling term and holiday.
